text:
Gabriel Vilardi has one goal in 18 games, and he's apologized for it (TSN). The number is ugly. The process behind it isn't. He has 5.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 2.9% against a normal range of 12 to 17%, and Winnipeg has scored 6.2 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. That is about as unlucky as a top-six forward gets.

His ice time is up two minutes over the last ten games, and Scott Arniel reunited him with Kyle Connor and Mark Scheifele to restart the offense (TSN). It has worked for the team, three straight wins, even if it hasn't worked for his goal column yet: he has an assist in each of the last three games.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.4 scoring chances per 60 from right in front of the net last season, 99th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among forwards in wins above replacement. Players who live in that area don't stay at one goal. We'd expect a cluster soon.
